data_notes: Data has been recorded for different purposes. In a different User Study (User Study 1, the data collected was used to compare the multi-phalanx approach with a single-phalanx method. Multimodal Sensing and Modeling of Endocrine Therapy Adherence in Breast Cancer Survivors. Proc. ACM Interact. Mob. Wearable Ubiquitous Technol. 9, 4, Article 236 (December 2025), 33 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3770864
code_notes: The authors release complete source code and documentation replicating preprocessing, modeling, and evaluation.
data_notes: The multimodal dataset cannot be publicly released due to IRB restrictions; The authors state that researchers may contact the corresponding author to discuss potential options for data access.
hardware_notes: Requires Fitbit Sense smartwatches, RxCap MEMS pill bottles with the RxCap Engage system, and participants smartphones.
software_notes: Uses proprietary Fitabase and RxCap Engage platforms together with Python-based machine learning tools.
instructions_notes: A public GitHub repository with code and documentation is provided to replicate preprocessing, modeling, and evaluation steps.

title: Translation of Radar Signals into Latent Cardiac Event Space for Scalable, Annotation-free Heart Disease Diagnosis
citation: AoXiang Yue, Zhi Lu, Yang Hu, Zhenzhen Cao, and Yan Chen. 2025. Translation of Radar Signals into Latent Cardiac Event Space for Scalable, Annotation-free Heart Disease Diagnosis. Proc. ACM Interact. Mob. Wearable Ubiquitous Technol. 9, 4, Article 237 (December 2025), 30 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3770693
code_notes: No code repository or download link is mentioned.
data_notes: The method requires both a large publicly available multi-dataset ECG corpus and the authors own radar–ECG clinical dataset, but only the external ECG datasets are publicly available.
hardware_notes: Requires a self-designed FMCW radar platform; NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU; and a clinical 12-lead ECG system deployed in hospital wards and clinics.
software_notes: Models are trained using PyTorch with the Adam optimizer and other standard deep learning tools.
instructions_notes: Paper specifies radar configuration, dataset splits, network architecture, and training hyperparameters but does not provide a runnable code repository or step-by-step execution commands.

title: PocketMap: An Interaction-centric 3D Map Serving System for Spatial Understanding on Mobile Devices
citation: Xinran Zhang, Wuyang Zhang, Hanqi Zhu, Yifan Duan, Jianmin Ji, and Yanyong Zhang. 2025. PocketMap: An Interaction-centric 3D Map Serving System for Spatial Understanding on Mobile Devices. Proc. ACM Interact. Mob. Wearable Ubiquitous Technol. 9, 4, Article 238 (December 2025), 28 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3770680
code_notes: No code repository or download link is mentioned.
data_notes: Uses two public 3D reconstruction benchmarks (Complex-campus and Structured-city) and two real-world datasets (Green-park and Glass-hall) that are not released.
hardware_notes: Requires a server workstation and a client device such as an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier or smartphone to run PocketMap and collect images in the four environments.
software_notes: Implements PocketMap in Python using 3D Gaussian Splatting, COLMAP, YOLOv9, SAM, Depth Anything V2, StableNormal, OpenCV, and the proprietary GPT-4o API for LLM-based prompt parsing.
instructions_notes: The paper details the system architecture, modules, datasets, and experimental setup but provides no installation or run commands or code repository.

title: VibeAlign: Maximizing Variation of Heart Beat in CSI of COTS Wi-Fi Devices via Signal Alignment
citation: Youwei Zhang, Zhi Liu, and Suhua Tang. 2025. VibeAlign: Maximizing Variation of Heart Beat in CSI of COTS Wi-Fi Devices via Signal Alignment. Proc. ACM Interact. Mob. Wearable Ubiquitous Technol. 9, 4, Article 239 (December 2025), 31 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3770704
code_notes: No source code URL or repository is provided.
data_notes: The paper does not provide a public download link for the CSI or ECG datasets used in the experiments.
hardware_notes: Uses COTS WiFi transceivers with Intel 5300 NICs, directional and omni antennas, mini-PCs, and a Polar H10 heart rate strap for ground truth.
software_notes: MATLAB R2021B; CSI-Tool for data collection.
instructions_notes: Paper describes the algorithm and experimental setup but provides no step-by-step implementation or run commands.

title: MagSkin: Enabling Touchless Human-Computer Interaction with Soft Epidermal Magnetic Material
citation: Zeyu Zhang, Hua Huang, Penghao Dong, Shanshan Yao, and Shan Lin. 2025. MagSkin: Enabling Touchless Human-Computer Interaction with Soft Epidermal Magnetic Material. Proc. ACM Interact. Mob. Wearable Ubiquitous Technol. 9, 4, Article 240 (December 2025), 30 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3770675
code_notes: No source code or repository link is provided.
data_notes: Evaluation uses MagSkin datasets collected from volunteers, but no dataset download link is provided.
hardware_notes: Requires custom soft magnetic skin worn on the fingertip, a smartphone magnetometer, a 3D positioning system with robotic arm, and a Hall gaussmeter for evaluation.
software_notes: Uses Ansys Maxwell for magnetic field simulation and standard machine learning tools for gesture classification.
instructions_notes: The paper details models, algorithms, and experimental setup but provides no step-by-step implementation or run commands.

title: Biobehavioral Rhythms in Everyday Life: Data and Models for Capturing Cyclic Behavior in Naturalistic Settings
citation: Chong Zhao, Maria Ana Cardei, Matthew Clark, Runze Yan, and Afsaneh Doryab. 2025. Biobehavioral Rhythms in Everyday Life: Data and Models for Capturing Cyclic Behavior in Naturalistic Settings. Proc. ACM Interact. Mob. Wearable Ubiquitous Technol. 9, 4, Article 241 (December 2025), 36 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3770698
code_notes: The official Human Rhythms Dataset repository includes rhythms_cosinor.py for rhythm analysis.
data_notes: Provides the Human Rhythms Dataset with raw sensor data, derived behavioral features, rhythm parameters, and external context files via GitHub.
hardware_notes: Uses Fitbit Sense wearables and participants smartphones running the AWARE mobile sensing app for passive data collection.
software_notes: Data analysis uses Python libraries (RAPIDS, CosinorPy); data collection used the open-source AWARE framework.
instructions_notes: The paper and dataset README describe sensing setup and dataset usage but do not provide end-to-end installation or run commands.

title: SpikeTouch: Optimizing Spike Neural Networks for Tactile Perception
citation: Xuerong Zhao, Xuan Wang, Jian Wu, Chao Feng, Dingyi Fang, Xiaojiang Chen, and Zheng Wang. 2025. SpikeTouch: Optimizing Spike Neural Networks for Tactile Perception. Proc. ACM Interact. Mob. Wearable Ubiquitous Technol. 9, 4, Article 242 (December 2025), 24 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3770658
code_notes: No source code repository or implementation link for SpikeTouch is provided.
data_notes: Tactile datasets collected from 20 volunteers with a pressure-sensor glove are used but not released for public download.
hardware_notes: Requires a flexible glove with pressure sensors (RX-G0505M), the Tianjic neuromorphic chip (Lynxi HS140 platform) and a PC with an NVIDIA RTX 2080Ti GPU for training.
software_notes: Uses proprietary tools such as MATLAB, the LynSDK software stack, and the Lyngor graphical programming framework in addition to Python and PyTorch.
instructions_notes: The paper details system design, hyperparameters, and deployment setup but does not provide runnable code, installation instructions, or step-by-step commands.

title: From Motion to Localization: Cross-view Optimization with Stationary Event and RGB Cameras for Enhanced Pose Estimation
citation: Yukun Zhao, Xinyuan Song, Huajian Huang, and Tristan Braud. 2025. From Motion to Localization: Cross-view Optimization with Stationary Event and RGB Cameras for Enhanced Pose Estimation. Proc. ACM Interact. Mob. Wearable Ubiquitous Technol. 9, 4, Article 243 (December 2025), 25 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3770631
code_notes: The authors state they open source the implementation code, but no repository URL is provided in the text.
data_notes: Authors contribute a new cross-view pose estimation dataset but do not provide a public download link.
hardware_notes: Requires a stationary sensing platform (Sony camera, RGB camera, Livox Avia LiDAR, NUC mini-computer) and a user device (iPhone 16 Pro); server uses NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090.
software_notes: Uses proprietary ARKit 5.1.5 for the data capture app, Metavision SDK, and Halcon software, with the EVS-CVPO pipeline implemented in PyTorch.
instructions_notes: The paper describes the sensing platform, dataset collection, and algorithms but does not provide runnable code, installation instructions, or step-by-step commands.
